opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the role owns the Payroll system, the maximum access level is admin. Requested write access is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 as a contractor with basic security training (note: HR listed full-time). As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed access is read. Requested write exceeds this maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The HR note lists E031 as full-time Payroll Specialist, but the Security note reports the Security DB shows E031 as a contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor classification, the maximum allowed access is read (write requires advanced training). Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, the maximum is granted: read. I am following the security database's employee classification as it directly contradicts the HR note.
